source_text: Principium Levitici: vocavit Dominus Moysen et locutus est ei de tabernaculo. Vocatio Dei ad secreta ducit. Non in Aegypto vocatur ad sacrificia, sed in deserto, in tabernaculo testimonii. Qui adhuc in Aegypto vitiorum est, hostias spiritales offerre non potest. Vocatus Moyses legem sacrificiorum accipit — non ut cruentis victimis Christum ecclesia immolet, sed ut intelligat holocaustum rationabile.
orientation: Origen is beginning his homily on Leviticus 1:1, explaining that God's call to Moses from the tabernacle is a call to spiritual understanding, not to literal sacrifice.
pass_a_gloss: Beginning [of] Leviticus: [he] called [the] Lord Moses and [he] spoke [is] to him from [the] tabernacle. [The] calling [of] God to secret [places] leads. Not in Egypt [he] is called to sacrifices, but in [the] desert, in [the] tabernacle [of] testimony. [He] who still in Egypt [of] vices is, sacrifices spiritual to offer not [he] is able. [Having been] called Moses [the] law [of] sacrifices receives — not so that with bloody victims Christ [the] church may sacrifice, but so that [she] may understand [the] holocaust reasonable.

choices.why: Renders the opening phrase as a heading-like statement, matching the source's simple noun phrase.

choices.english: The call of God leads to secret things
choices.why: Keeps the present tense and the abstract noun 'call' as subject, preserving the aphoristic force.
rejected: God's call leads to hidden things
The divine call leads to mysteries

choices.english: in the desert, in the tabernacle of testimony
choices.why: Preserves the double locative phrase and the literal 'tabernacle of testimony' as in the source.
rejected: in the wilderness, in the tent of witness
in the desert, in the tent of meeting

choices.why: Keeps the genitive metaphor 'Egypt of vices' exactly, which is central to Origen's moral allegory.
Uses the glossary term 'spiritual' for spiritales and 'sacrifices' for hostias, matching the brief's required vocabulary.
Uses the glossary term 'burnt offering' for holocaustum and keeps 'reasonable' for rationabile, echoing Romans 12:1's 'reasonable service'.

bible_refs.note: The Lord called Moses and spoke to him from the tabernacle

pass_b_english: The beginning of Leviticus: the Lord called Moses and spoke to him from the tabernacle. The call of God leads to secret things. He is not called to sacrifices in Egypt, but in the desert, in the tabernacle of testimony. Whoever is still in the Egypt of vices cannot offer spiritual sacrifices. Moses is called and receives the law of sacrifices — not so that the church may sacrifice Christ with bloody victims, but so that it may understand the reasonable burnt offering.

last_rejected.why: "Rationabile" means rational/spiritual (LXX λογικόν), not "reasonable" in modern sense.
last_rejected.fix: rational burnt offering or spiritual burnt offering
last_rejected.ruling: "Reasonable" is a valid traditional rendering of rationabile (λογικόν); not a modern sense error.

last_rejected.why: "Immolet" means slay/immolate, not "sacrifice" as general offering; misses violent sacrificial death.
last_rejected.fix: slay Christ with bloody victims or immolate Christ with bloody victims
last_rejected.ruling: "Sacrifice" correctly renders immolet; "bloody victims" conveys the violent sacrificial death.
